newsitem.title: germany: Police probe blast at Dresdner Bank branch.
newsitem.headline: Police probe blast at Dresdner Bank branch.

text.p: An explosive device heavily damaged a branch of Dresdner Bank in western Germany early on Monday, police said.

Police were investigating whether steel workers angered by Dresdner's backing of a controversial corporate takeover bid had been behind the attack in the town of Hattingen, but said they had found no indication of political motives.

The attackers had detonated the device in a night safe for after-hours cash deposits at the branch's entrance, police said. Much of the bank's glass entrance was shattered and the windows of buildings opposite were pockmarked by flying debris.

A police spokesman said witnesses had seen two men running away after the explosion in the entrance to the branch and it was possible they had been trying to get at cash deposited in the night safe. He said they escaped empty-handed.
Trade unions sharply criticised Dresdner Bank last week because its investment banking unit was helping to finance a hostile takeover bid for steel firm Thyssen by rival Krupp.
The takeover was expected to cost thousands of jobs in Germany's steel-and-coal Ruhr Valley heartland and prompted a wave of outrage and industrial stoppages.
After Krupp's takeover plans caused an uproar, the company agreed to hold talks with Thyssen to see if it could increase steel cooperation to avert an all-out hostile takeover.
But Krupp has vowed to relaunch its bid if the talks do not produce a satisfactory result. Eight days of talks at a secret location are expected to end on Thursday.
Police said the attack in Hattingen, which is close to the city of Essen where Krupp has its headquarters, occurred at 4.16 a.m. (0316 GMT).
